rows.title: SNN output feedback loop
rows.intent: Let a human reviewer decide whether spiking-network results should become provenance-carrying ledger rows that both the triad stack and the nets can query.
rows.beneficiary: the operator and reviewers deciding on it; future agents and SNN experiments that would query shared results
rows.divergence: Today the dependency runs one way (as the suggestion describes it: the SNN reads the covenant, and the covenant records nothing from SNN runs); this would add a write-back path from SNN outputs into the ledger.
rows.diverges_from: current one-way SNN-to-covenant dependency, as described in the suggestion text (not independently measured in this record)
rows.sequencing: Engineering regardless of the selectivity trial outcome (per the sequencing note). Independent of the ledger and triad work.
rows.effect: none until adopted by human review; no rule, gate, code path, anchor or protected block is changed by this row

rows.words: 1. SNN output feedback loop: spiking-experiments network outputs (firing rates, weight trajectories, failed-run signatures) should write back to the covenant ledger as rows carrying intent, beneficiary, and divergence. This flips the current one-way dependency (SNN reads covenant; covenant knows nothing of spikes) into shared scientific memory queryable by both the triad stack and the nets.

rows.title: Flinch-as-bridge protocol
rows.intent: Let a human reviewer decide whether SNN run aborts and anomalous selectivity should be handled by the existing sealed, preregistered, blind-scored flinch-observability process instead of a new anomaly detector.
rows.beneficiary: the operator and reviewers deciding on it; the SNN experiments and the flinch-observability record, which would share one scoring discipline
rows.divergence: No current path registers SNN run aborts or anomalous selectivity patterns as flinch-observability events; this would add one, reusing existing flinch infrastructure.
rows.diverges_from: current practice: SNN aborts and anomalies are not registered as flinch-observability events (as implied by the suggestion text; not independently measured in this record)
rows.sequencing: Engineering regardless of the selectivity trial outcome (per the sequencing note). Independent of the ledger and triad work.
rows.effect: none until adopted by human review; no rule, gate, code path, anchor or protected block is changed by this row

rows.words: 2. Flinch-as-bridge protocol: SNN run aborts and anomalous selectivity patterns should register as flinch-observability events — sealed, preregistered, blindly scored — reusing existing flinch infrastructure rather than building new anomaly detection.

rows.title: Competing-neurons to multi-agent legs prior
rows.intent: Hold a conditional design prior for the multi-agent legs framework so that it can be reviewed only if the preregistered selectivity trial produces the stated result.
rows.beneficiary: the operator and reviewers deciding on it; the multi-agent legs framework, if the trial result supports it
rows.divergence: The multi-agent legs framework currently has no empirical prior drawn from SNN results; if the trial condition is met and the row is adopted, lateral inhibition would be treated as a design principle across substrates rather than a metaphor.
rows.diverges_from: current multi-agent legs framework design, which takes no prior from SNN selectivity results
rows.conditional_on: the preregistered eight-seed selectivity trial showing competing neurons beat isolated ones. No such result is claimed or recorded here.
rows.sequencing: Conditional on the selectivity trial result (per the sequencing note). It has no effect unless that result is measured and reviewed. Independent of the ledger and triad work.
rows.effect: none: conditional, and has no effect unless the trial result is measured and reviewed and the row is then adopted by human review; no rule, gate, code path, anchor or protected block is changed by this row

Competing-neurons to multi-agent legs prior: if the preregistered eight-seed selectivity trial shows competing neurons beat isolated ones, that measured result becomes an empirical prior for the multi-agent legs framework (rotating model instances that offset each other), treating lateral inhibition as a design principle across substrates rather than a metaphor.
